segments.he: יַעֲקב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית שֶׁגַּם בְּעמֶק הַחֹשֶׁךְ יִצְעֲקוּ אֶל
segments.en: For Haman cast lots from day to day and from month to month — twelve months — seeking to bring them down from day to day and month to month until they fell completely, to destroy, kill and annihilate them, Heaven forbid. For such is the way of the evil inclination: today it says "do a little," one sin draws another — the aspect of "those who drag iniquity with cords of falsehood" [Yeshayahu 5:18]. And in truth, according to the way of the evil inclination with people who do not overpower it in their youth, there would certainly be no hope for most of the world. But Hashem has compassion upon His people Yisrael in every generation and "devises plans so that no one be cast off from Him" [Shmuel II 14:14] — and He sends help from Above through wondrous ways, through the great true Tzaddikim of the generation.

segments.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת. כִּי תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית הִוא מַה שֶׁתִּקֵּן יַעֲקב אָבִינוּ לְהִתְחַזֵּק בִּתְפִלָּה אֲפִלּוּ מִתּוֹךְ עמֶק הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁהוּא בְּתֹקֶף מְרִירַת הַגָּלוּת בְּגוּף וְנֶפֶשׁ וְכוּ' כַּנַּ"ל שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר בִּנְיַן בַּיִת הַשְּׁלִישִׁי שֶׁאָנוּ מְקַוִּים שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִבְנֶה בִּזְכוּת יַעֲקב וְכוּ' כַּנַּ"ל. וְעַל כֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת. וְלִכְאוֹרָה קָשֶׁה אִם כֵּן כְּשֶׁזּאת הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית הִיא רְשׁוּת אִם כֵּן מַה תִּקֵּן יַעֲקב אָבִינוּ. וְכִי יַעֲלֶה עַל הַדַּעַת שֶׁיֵּשׁ אִסּוּר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בַּלַּיְלָה. אַךְ יַעֲקב אָבִינוּ צָפָה וְרָאָה עמֶק אֲרִיכַת הַגָּלוּת הַמַּר הַזֶּה אֵיךְ הַסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתְפַּשֵּׁט מְאד מְאד בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת חֶשְׁכַת לַיְלָה כַּנַּ"ל. וְהוּא בְּעצֶם כּחוֹ תִּקֵּן שֶׁגַּם אָז נוּכַל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וְלָשׁוּב אֶל ה' שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית כַּנַּ"ל. אֲבָל רָאָה שֶׁמֵּעצֶם מְרִירַת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא וְהַקְּלִפּוֹת עַל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן לְהַטִּיל עָלָיו חִיּוּב לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אָז.
segments.en: And this is the aspect of Mordechai, who immediately sensed the intent of the Sitra Achra — which is the aspect of Haman — in the aspect of: "Mordechai knew all that had been done" [Esther 4:1], for he knew their intent to the very end. And he immediately begins to arouse them to teshuvah: "he went out into the midst of the city and cried out a great and bitter cry" [ibid.]. And the essence of his crying out was to inform Esther — who is the aspect of the collective of Yisrael — not yet to despair of mercy, and to come before the King however she is, even though she is far from Him, not having been called to Him for thirty days — which is the totality of the month, the minimum that Yisrael should present themselves before their Father in Heaven at least once a month. But sometimes they are so distanced that they do not merit even that — in the aspect of: "I have not been called" [Esther 4:11]. Even so, one must knock on the doors of mercy — perhaps He will take pity, perhaps He will have compassion. And so Esther afterward agreed with Mordechai and said: "and so I will go before the King, which is not according to the law" [ibid. 4:16]. As our Rabbis taught: not according to the law of the Torah — for I know within myself that according to the law of the Torah I am certainly not worthy to come before the King to pray before Him, given what I know of my sins and transgressions. Nevertheless I will come before Him not according to the law — and "if I perish, I perish": if, Heaven forbid, my prayers and hisbodidus before Him find no favor due to the multitude of my corruptions — as I have perished through my evil deeds, so I have perished. Hashem will do with me as He wishes. Yet I will always hope and cry out to Hashem — perhaps He will have mercy. And then Hashem had compassion on Mordechai and his people — and the drawing-close from Hashem that sometimes reaches a person of very low standing, that even so Hashem sends closeness from afar — this is the secret of the extending of the golden sceptre that miraculously stretched many cubits, as our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded.

segments.he: כִּי אָז בִּבְחִינַת תּקֶף מְרִירַת חֶשְׁכַת לַיְלָה הוּא בִּבְחִינַת הֶעְדֵּר הַדִּבּוּר בְּחִינַת יוֹנָה אִלֶּמֶת בְּחִינַת נֶאְלַמְתִּי לא אֶפְתַּח פִּי בְּחִינַת נֶאְלַמְתִּי דּוּמִיָּה הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי מִטּוֹב וְכוּ' שֶׁזֶּה נֶאֱמַר עַל זְמַן הַגָּלוּת. עַד שֶׁלּוּלֵי כּחַ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים בְּחִינַת יַעֲקב כְּבָר הָיוּ הַכּל מִתְיָאֲשִׁים לְגַמְרֵי מִלְּהִתְפַּלֵּל וְלָשׁוּב אָז בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תְּהוֹמוֹת רָעִים וְכוּ' כָּאֵלֶּה. וְזֶה תִּקֵּן יַעֲקב אָבִינוּ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כְּלַל הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ יָצְאוּ כֻּלָּם.
segments.en: This is the aspect of "from the straits I called to G-d" [Tehillim 118:5]. And it is explained in the kavanos that meitzar [straits] is the letters of tzemer [wool] — the aspect of the hairs of the beard [dikna] which are the aspect of the Tikunei Dikna. That is, as explained above, the hairs of the holy beard — which are all the attributes of compassion — are drawn through the aspect of "from the straits I called to G-d." For when a person detaches himself even by a hair's breadth from his material nature toward Hashem — that is, when he is in great straits and the desires and the Sitra Achra overpower him as they overpower, until he has no way to turn right or left, in the aspect of: "all who pursued her overtook her in the straits" [Eichah 1:3] — until it seems there is no hope, Heaven forbid. And yet in the very depth of his pressure and the straits of his soul, he turns to Hashem and cries out to Him from the straits, in the aspect of "from the straits I called to G-d." Even though what he turns toward Hashem is only like a hair's breadth — it is exceedingly precious in Hashem's eyes. And from the meitzar [straits] emerges tzemer [wool] — which is the aspect of the hairs of the holy beard where all is compassion and goodness, where everything is turned to good and merit.

segments.he: שֶׁבְּעצֶם כּחוֹ תִּקֵּן תַּקָּנוֹת נִפְלָאוֹת וְנוֹרָאוֹת מְאד בְּעֵת שֶׁלָּן שָׁם בַּמָּקוֹם הַהוּא וְיָרַד לְמָקוֹם שֶׁיָּרַד בְּעֵת שְׁנָתוֹ וּמִשָּׁם עָלָה לְמָקוֹם שֶׁעָלָה עַד שֶׁתִּקֵּן שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ בְּחֶשְׁכַת לַיְלָה וַאֲפֵלָה מַמָּשׁ יִתְעוֹרֵר הָאָדָם בִּרְצוֹנוֹת חֲזָקִים לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וְלָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלא יִתְיָאֵשׁ מִן הַתְּפִלָּה וְהַצְּעָקָה לְעוֹלָם. כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִזְהִיר אֲדוֹנֵנוּ מוֹרֵנוּ וְרַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה וְאָמַר רַק שֶׁלּא יִתְיָאֵשׁ מִן הַצְּעָקָה וְהַתְּפִלָּה. (אַבִּי מֶע אִיז זִיךְ נִיט מְיָאֵשׁ פוּן שְׁרַיֶיאן מֶע שְׁרַייט מֶע בֵּייט וְכוּ') וְאָז הַכּל מִתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹבָה וְכוּ'. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת שֶׁתִּקֵּן יַעֲקב אָבִינוּ כִּי קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקב הַמֻּשְׁרָשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבָּא מִזַּרְעוֹ הוּא בְּחִינַת נְקֻדַּת הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רָצוֹן שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אוֹר הַפָּנִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקב בְּחִינַת מְבַקְשֵׁי פָנֶיךָ יַעֲקב סֶלָה. עַל כֵּן יַעֲקב אָבִינוּ בְּעצֶם כּחוֹ הִכְנִיס בְּלֵב כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד סוֹף הַדּוֹרוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים הָאֵלֶּה שֶׁהֵם עִקְּבוֹת מְשִׁיחָא שֶׁגַּם עַתָּה בִּמְרִירוּת הַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תּקֶף חֶשְׁכַת לַיְלָה יִסְתַּכֵּל כָּל אֶחָד עַל הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ עַד שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יִתְחַזֵּק מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא בִּרְצוֹנוֹת חֲזָקִים וְכִסּוּפִין טוֹבִים לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְחִינַת זָכַרְתִּי בַּלַּיְלָה שִׁמְךָ ה' בְּחִינַת אֶזְכְּרָה נְגִינָתִי בַּלָּיְלָה עִם לְבָבִי אָשִׂיחָה וִיחַפֵּשׂ רוּחִי מַה יִּהְיֶה הַסּוֹף וְהַתַּכְלִית מִמֶּנִּי בְּחִינַת עַל מִשְׁכָּבִי בַּלֵּילוֹת בִּקַּשְׁתִּי אֶת שֶׁאָהֲבָה נַפְשִׁי. שֶׁיִּתְחַזֵּק גַּם אָז לְחַפֵּשׂ וּלְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת שֶׁאָהֲבָה נַפְשִׁי שֶׁהִיא קְדֻשַּׁת יַהֲדוּתוֹ וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִמְצא בְּחִינַת בִּקַּשְׁתִּיו וְלא מְצָאתִיו. אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אָקוּמָה נָא וַאֲסֹבְבָה בָּעִיר וּבָרְחוֹבוֹת וּבַשְּׁוָקִים וְכוּ'. וְזֶה עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁתִּקֵּן יַעֲקב אָבִינוּ שֶׁגַּם בְּתֹקֶף חֶשְׁכַת לַיְלָה בְּחִינַת אֲרִיכַת הַגָּלוּת נְבַקֵּשׁ וּנְחַפֵּשׂ אֶת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּרְצוֹנוֹת חֲזָקִים מְאד עַד שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא יִתְחַזֵּק לִפְתּחַ פִּיו בְּדִבּוּרֵי תְּפִלָּה גַּם אָז בִּבְחִינַת נֶאְלַמְתִּי דּוּמִיָּה הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי מִטּוֹב וּכְאֵבִי נֶעְכָּר חַם לִבִּי בְּקִרְבִּי בַּהֲגִיגִי תִּבְעַר אֵשׁ דִּבַּרְתִּי בִלְשׁוֹנִי. וּבֶאֱמֶת בְּחִינַת דֶּרֶךְ זֶה הוּא עִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הַתְּפִלָּה תָּמִיד. וְזֶה עִקַּר הָעֵצָה לִתְפִלָּה וְשִׂיחָה וְהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר): כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וּלְפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי רְצוֹנוֹת טוֹבִים וְכִסּוּפִים וְכוּ'. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת אַל תַּעַשׂ תְּפִלָּתְךָ קֶבַע וְכוּ'. רַק שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי כֵן בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לְתַקֵּן תְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיוּ חוֹבָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַהֲמוֹן עַם כִּי בְּלא זֶה לא יִתְפַּלְּלוּ כְּלָל. אֲבָל יַעֲקב שֶׁהוֹרִיד אֶת עַצְמוֹ עַד הַסּוֹף עַד עִקְּבוֹת מְשִׁיחָא הוּא עָסַק בְּעִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת שֶׁגַּם בְּעמֶק הַחֹשֶׁךְ הִכְנִיס לְבַל יִתְיָאֵשׁ מִן הַתְּפִלָּה רַק יִתְחַזֵּק בִּרְצוֹנוֹת חֲזָקִים לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַד שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר מֵעַצְמוֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר תִּקּוּן הַתְּפִלָּה כַּנַּ"ל. (שָׁם אוֹת פ"ט):
segments.en: For the primary deveykus and closeness to Hashem is through voices — which are the aspect of the ten kinds of melody, in which all voices in the world are included. Through them is the primary closeness of Yisrael to their Father in Heaven. For all the prayers and songs and praises and supplications and petitions and confessions and appeasements and all the conversations a person conducts between himself and his Maker in hisbodidus — all is included within the ten kinds of melody, which are the ten forms of expression in which the Book of Tehillim was said. As our Rabbis taught [Pesachim 117]: "with a psalm, with a victory, with melody..." as explained in the words of Rabbainu of blessed memory [Likutay Moharan 205] regarding the ten chapters of Tehillim he revealed as a remedy for a nocturnal occurrence — see there. And it is well known that the Book of Tehillim encompasses all forms of prayer and supplication, for most of Tehillim speaks of cries and outcries and pleas to Hashem and many forms of supplication that Hashem help one do His will and emerge from the depths of the sea of worldly desires and vanities. And within these cries and supplications of King Dovid, he begins to sing and praise and give thanks and glorify Hashem. And all these holy ways and paths of the Book of Tehillim are the aspect of the ten kinds of melody — which is the aspect of the ten forms in which the Book of Tehillim was said — in which all petitions and songs and praises are included that all Yisrael recite wherever they are. For the primary closeness to Hashem is through this. As Rabbainu of blessed memory wrote [Likutay Moharan II:84]: Know that the primary bond and deveykus of Yisrael to Hashem is through prayer. It follows that the primary bond and deveykus of Yisrael to Hashem is through the holy voices of songs and praises and prayers and supplications and melodies and songs — all of which is the aspect of the ten kinds of melody through which is the primary closeness of Yisrael to their Father in Heaven.
